Modern.brandNameRationale: Charles Goodyear Jr.'s 1869 Goodyear welt machine mechanized the welted-construction shoe and defined quality footwear for 150 years. The technique is public-domain (the patent expired long ago); the surname refers to the technique, not to the tire company.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern footwear is split between fast-fashion sneakers and a small Goodyear-welted cohort. The opening is for a brand that anchors on the construction itself — resoleable, repairable, built to outlive a decade.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Allen Edmonds (allenedmonds.com) holds the American welted-shoe peer slot. Crockett & Jones (crockettandjones.com) is the British reference. Meermin (meermin.com) plays the value-Spanish position. We sit closer to Meermin in scale with sharper construction transparency.
Modern.positioningStatement: Modern Goodyear-welted footwear, resoleable for life.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Owns at least one good pair. Cares about construction over style. Will resole rather than replace.
behaviors: Reads the welt under the shoe
Buys one pair every three years

dos: Show the welt under the shoe

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Goodyear & Welt in a precise modern grotesk with the ampersand drawn slightly bolder. A small welt-line icon (a single stitch row) serves as the hangtag stamp.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for construction specs and resole receipts
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the technical data: size, last, construction.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: The Worshipful Company of Cordwainers is the London livery company chartered in 1439 — the medieval guild of fine-leather shoemakers (the name comes from 'Cordovan' leather of Córdoba). The guild and its standards are public-domain historical references.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury bespoke shoemaking is dominated by a few St. James's Street houses. The opening is for a brand that anchors on the medieval Cordwainer guild standards — livery-grade construction with documented provenance.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Crockett & Jones (crockettandjones.com) is the heritage-British peer. Edward Green (edwardgreen.com) holds the bespoke-British luxury slot. George Cleverley (gjcleverley.co.uk) is the bespoke-haute peer. We sit between Edward Green and Cleverley in posture.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Livery-grade luxury shoemaking in the Cordwainer guild tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 50 to 75. Owns at least three pairs of bespoke shoes. Has a personal last. Returns for service annually.

dos: Speak in the language of last, welt, and shell

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Cordwainer Hall set in a classical English roman with a small embossed guild mark depicting crossed awls. The mark appears on the order book, the brass plaque, and the inside lining.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and order book
typography.secondary: Söhne for the few digital surfaces
typography.rationale: Caslon carries the British livery tradition. Söhne handles correspondence.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: The plimsoll shoe (1830s) was named for the Plimsoll line on ship hulls because the rubber-canvas seam resembled it. It is the original minimal canvas sneaker. The word is the shoe.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal footwear has been crowded with rebranded white sneakers. The opening underneath is the original plimsoll silhouette — canvas upper, rubber sole, the simplest construction in modern footwear.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Veja (veja-store.com) holds the considered-minimal sneaker slot. Common Projects (commonprojects.com) is the minimal-luxury peer. Spring Court (springcourt.com) is the heritage-canvas reference. We sit closer to Spring Court with sharper construction discipline.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Minimal canvas-and-rubber footwear in the original plimsoll silhouette.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Owns three pairs of shoes. Will pay 2x for the right canvas. Replaces the same pair when it wears out.

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark — Plimsoll in a humanist sans, all lowercase, with a single horizontal line (the Plimsoll line) above. The line alone is the favicon.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and body
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for sizing tables
typography.rationale: One family. Mono for the dimensions.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Welted construction is the industry quality benchmark for resoleable shoes (distinct from cemented or Blake-stitched). The two words name the technique and the producer.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate-issue footwear is a serious B2B category. Hotel groups, hospitality chains, and uniformed services need durable, resoleable shoes specified by lifecycle cost rather than retail price.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Red Wing for Business (redwingforbusiness.com) holds the workwear B2B slot. Clarks Originals Trade (clarks.com) sits in the heritage-British peer position. Caterpillar Footwear (catfootwear.com) plays the industrial peer. We sit smaller and more welted-specific than these.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Welted footwear for hospitality and uniformed services — durable, resoleable, spec-grade.

targetAudience.primary: 40 to 60. Procurement directors at hotel groups, hospitality chains, and uniformed services. Sign multi-year supply contracts.

dos: Show the welt and the sole

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small welt-stitch mark — WELTED WORKS set in a tight grotesk above a single stitched line. Reads cleanly on spec sheets, name badges, and trade-show banners.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for spec sheets and RFPs
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed B2B documentation.

Creative.tagline: Under the patronage of the shoemaker-saints.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Saints Crispin and Crispinian were 3rd-century patron saints of shoemakers (their feast day, October 25, is the cobblers' holiday; Shakespeare's 'St. Crispin's Day' speech anchors the cultural memory). The names are public-domain religious-historical references.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative footwear has been crowded with novelty sneaker brands. The opening is for a house with deep symbolic anchoring — patron-saint iconography on every box, every pair.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Camper (camper.com) holds the Spanish-creative slot. Buttero (buttero.it) sits in the Italian-craft peer position. Feit (feitdirect.com) plays the small-batch peer. We sit closer to Feit with sharper iconographic grounding.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative footwear house under the patronage of the shoemaker-saints.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Design-literate buyer. Owns at least one pair of small-batch shoes. Cares about story as much as construction.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — Crispin & Crispinian set in a warm display serif with a small two-figure icon (the twin saints) above. The icon appears on every box and the inside lining.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and editorial
typography.secondary: PP Mori for body and product cards
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the manuscript register. Mori keeps product copy warm.
